stem.text: Light of a single wavelength is incident normally on a double slit. The slit separation can be varied.
A screen is placed a fixed distance away from the double slit. The screen and double slit are parallel. A pattern of bright interference fringes is observed on a screen.

stem.alt: Apparatus diagram: parallel arrows labelled light point to the right at a double slit drawn as two vertical barriers with a gap between them, labelled a with a dimension arrow across the slit separation. A vertical screen lies to the right, labelled screen. NOT TO SCALE is written at the upper right.

stem.text: Which graph best shows the variation of the separation $x$ of the bright interference fringes with the slit separation $a$?

A.alt: Graph with vertical axis labelled x and horizontal axis labelled a, origin marked 0. A curve starts near the vertical axis and falls towards the horizontal axis.

B.alt: Graph with vertical axis labelled x and horizontal axis labelled a, origin marked 0. A curve starts at the origin and rises steeply towards the right.

C.alt: Graph with vertical axis labelled x and horizontal axis labelled a, origin marked 0. A curve starts near the top of the vertical axis, stays high, then falls steeply towards the horizontal axis.

D.alt: Graph with vertical axis labelled x and horizontal axis labelled a, origin marked 0. A curve starts at the origin, rises steeply, then flattens as it moves to the right.
